doc.title: Chuck Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 7, 2023

chapter: Growing up in Verona and Dry Jack
title: Verona, drums and the road to fusion
summary: Rowe asks how Lamb and his brother came to fusion; Lamb began on drums at ten, played in bands with Rich, covering Jeff Beck and Yes.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Theoretical knowledge you mentioned — I’m curious because we go back a long ways and you come from a small town called Verona, New York, and I remember wondering back then seeing you in this band called Dry Jack, where did you and your brother, how did you come to this music, which at the time we would have — we’ll call it jazz fusion I guess.

Oh the fusion thing. You know man it was like playing — I started playing drums, you know that was my first axe. And then — when I was ten — and that was pretty much, that was it for me as far as the devotion to music. But Rich and I were in bands up until — like for fifteen years straight and we developed musically as we went along and started getting into — you know the fusion thing probably started with stuff we were doing cover tunes like Jeff Beck and we were doing, and then I was in a band called the Breakthrough with Rich and Gary Colmey and these Verona guys. And we did tunes by Yes, you know, and Yes was like, if you think about it, you know [scats]. Right? I mean that was like, I was really attracted to unison lines: bass player, guitar, bass, keyboard. I love that. And then that turned into hearing Chick Corea and his and the Seventh Galaxy. You know [scats] all that classic fusion stuff. And then we heard Return to Forever at here — at the chapel —
